Count the dotted blanks in fill-in exercises (the number of 'و'-joined groups) exactly as printed; do not add an extra blank.

This book prints fractions stacked (numerator over a horizontal rule), including the derivative operator د over د س — transcribe them as $\frac{...}{...}$, not as an inline solidus such as ٣/٢ or د / د س.

Unit-opener pages print two centred bold lines — أهداف الوحدة <N> then the chapter title — as one display block; both lines take `## `, never `### ` for the first.

observations: A bold, underlined line of the form `N/ <title> :` (e.g. `1/ الزمن الدوري :`, `3/ السرعة الزاوية :`) is a list item under the parenthesised section heading, not a heading — write it plain; only `(1-2-3)`-style section numbers take `###`.

This book writes the per-unit separator as a BACKSLASH, not a solidus: `1026م\ث`, `1 كم\ث`, `86646 كم\اليوم` (settled on p36 from the 2400 px crop `crops/36.tile1.webp`). The solidus is not bidi-mirrored, so the printed shape is the character — transcribe `\` and never normalise it to `/`.

A boxed or centred identity is stored in LOGICAL order, so the RIGHTMOST printed phrase comes FIRST in the Markdown line. On p36 the box is transcribed `قوة التثاقل = قوة الجذب المركزية   للأجرام السماوية والأقمار الإصطناعية`; the bold run sits against the right rule, and writing the line in the order the eye scans it left-to-right renders the box reversed.

Arabic symbols in this book's formulas carry subscripts drawn smaller and below the baseline (`ك_ق`, `ك_أ`, i.e. كق and كا) — keep them as `_` subscripts; flattening them to كق / كأ drops printed content.

A display equation with a side note (p36, `حيث نق هنا هي نصف قطر المسار الدائري للقمر .`) is set EQUATION FIRST — the equation stands to the right of the note — and its fractions carry the printed right-to-left order: `$\frac{ج ك_ق ك_أ}{نق^2} = \frac{ك_ق ع^2}{نق}$`. Table and figure caption lines printed bold above the grid keep their ** (they are captions), but a bold label that runs into its own sentence — تدريب : ، الحل : ، مثال (١) : — stays plain.

**p40 prints the ester general formula as `CnH₂nO₂` — the digits are subscripted, both n glyphs are full size on the baseline.** Transcribe `$CnH_2nO_2$` as printed; do not promote a letter index to a subscript to make a formula conventional.

**A prime after a radical letter is real print, not a scan scratch.** p40 draws `R – C – OR′` (thin slanted cap-height stroke after OR), corroborated by the cell's own line `جذران متشابهان أو مختلفان`. Keep the prime; both independent reads dropped it.

A lesson opener is three separate centred bold blue lines — `الدرس <ordinal>`, the numbered lesson title, and its English title — and each of the three takes `### `. `## ` is reserved for the book's 9 chapter titles, so a lesson opener never takes `## ` and the ordinal line is never left as a plain bold run.

Latin and digit runs embedded in Arabic lines are printed in VISUAL order by the source's bidi engine, so the glyph order on the page is not the order to type: the page draws `( 7- 1 )` for logical `(1 -7 )` and `(OH–)` for logical `(–OH)`. Always store the logical string that reproduces the printed glyph order, never the glyph order itself.
The book spells the English name of the carboxylic-acids lesson `Carboxilic Acids` — keep the printed spelling.

Section, example, figure and experiment numbers are Latin digits in CHAPTER-FIRST order: (1-8-2) is chapter 1, lesson 8, section 2; مثال (1 – 30) is chapter 1, example 30; likewise شكل (3 – 1) and التجربة (3-14) in chapter 3. A read that puts the item number first ((2-8-1), (30 -1)) has reversed the run — transcribe chapter-first, and check the run against the lesson ordinal printed on the page (الدرس الثامن → middle digit 8).

An English gloss printed on its own centred line under a lesson title — (Esters) under الخواص الفيزيائية والكيميائية للإسترات — stays inline at the end of that ### heading. It is not a heading of its own.
A lesson opener (الدرس الثامن, الدرس الثالث …) is ###, never ##. Only the book's 9 chapter titles take ##.

Section and example numbers in this book are chapter-first — (1-9), (1-9-1), مثال (1-33). A two-part number is drawn as `( 9-1)` and `(33 -1)` because the print's dash resolves as a neutral in the RTL line; transcribe the logical order, chapter digit first, and never store the order the eye scans.
Structural formulae and reaction equations are not tables — write them as `$$…$$` LaTeX arrays with `\mid` for the drawn vertical bonds; never a Markdown table or an ASCII pipe drawing.
This book writes يعتر for يعتبر (p85) — transcribe the printed form, never restore the ب.
The same paragraph on p85 spells the same word باحدى once and باحدي the next line; reproduce each occurrence as drawn rather than picking one form.
The book prints بنتج (single dot, initial ba) where ينتج is meant, in an exercise stem — keep the single-dot form exactly as drawn; do not restore the ya.
Chemical formulae whose subscripts are printed as true subscripts (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) are transcribed as LaTeX — $CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$ — never with Unicode subscript digits.

**A multiplication is printed with its SECOND factor leftmost.** p215 proves it with words: the percentage formula prints `100 × الكتلة النقية` with the Arabic phrase rightmost, so the logical order is `الكتلة النقية × 100`. Store the RIGHTMOST printed factor FIRST — `0.2 × 45`, `0.45 × 100` — even though the page shows `45 × 0.2` and `100 × 0.45`.

**A hyphenated digit pair is NOT mirrored.** `مثال (4-27)`, `مثال (4-28)`: the pair is a single left-to-right number run, so transcribe the digits in the order they appear left to right (chapter first). Do not reverse it the way a × expression must be reversed.

**Decimal notation is mixed inside a single page.** p215 carries `0.009`, `0.045`, `0.45`, `0.5` (dot, leading zero) alongside `,009` and `,45` (comma, no leading zero) for the same quantities. Reproduce each occurrence exactly as drawn — never normalise in either direction, and do not read the earlier comma observation as a rule that the book always uses commas.
**The percent sign prints to the LEFT of its number** (`٪` then `90` left to right), so it is written after the number with a space: `90 ٪`. An unspaced `90%` renders on the wrong side of the digits.

A worked example's stated ΔH and the number it then divides do not always agree — p244 states `ΔH = - 184.7 KJ` and the solution divides `– 185` to reach `– 92.5`. Transcribe each figure as drawn; never reconcile the solution against the statement.

This book prints its section and figure numbers with the CHAPTER DIGIT LAST — the thermochemistry chapter heads a subsection `(3-3-5)` and its figure `شكل (3-5)`. Transcribe the printed order with ASCII hyphens and never reorder it to chapter-first.

A hyphenated section or figure number is ONE identifier: store it exactly as it reads left to right on the page (`(3-5)`, `(3-3-5)`). Operands around an `X` or an `=` are SEPARATE terms on a right-to-left line: store them rightmost-printed-first, like every other token on the line (`س   = 30 X 462.3 = 13869.0`). Confusing the two is the one place two independent reads of this book mirror each other.
**Decimal separators switch inside a single worked example.** p263 prints `4.6` with a period two lines above `2,16` with a comma. Keep each occurrence as drawn; do not unify them.
**The multiplication sign is sometimes a capital Latin `X`.** p263 prints `2,16 X 10⁻⁶` and `4.6×10⁻⁶` on the same page. Transcribe the glyph actually drawn — never turn the `X` into `×` or `\times`.

**Unit exponents are typed inconsistently.** The same unit appears as `مول/دسم³` with a true superscript and as `مول/دسم3` with a baseline 3, sometimes within one equation line (p263). Reproduce each occurrence as drawn; decide superscript-vs-baseline by comparing the digit with the ordinary digits beside it in the same numerator, on a native-density crop.

**A minute-to-second denominator carries the printed order, even though the product is unchanged.** p263 sets the elapsed time rightmost, transcribed `180 × 60` and `(1440 - 360) × 60 ثانية`. Read the order off the page rather than assuming the conversion factor comes first.

Figure and example numbers in this book are set in Latin digits with the chapter component printed LEFTMOST — the page shows شكل (8-10) and مثال (8-12) in chapter 8. A hyphen-joined digit pair is a single left-to-right bidi run, so transcribe it in the printed pixel order; never reverse it to (10-8) / (12-8) to 'match' Arabic reading order.

Apparatus diagrams in chapter 8 carry small single-letter tube labels (ا، ب) set much smaller than the Arabic labels around them — they are easy to miss at page density but are real printed labels and belong in the label list in reading order.

Exercise sub-items in this book's end-of-chapter questions are numbered with Latin roman numerals followed by a closing parenthesis (i) ii) iii)) — keep the parenthesis on every one, including the first, which is easy to lose at page-render density.
p14 prints (بروميد الايثيل) with a bare alef — no hamza — in the common-naming example column; both independent reads restored the hamza to الأيثيل. Transcribe the bare alef as drawn.

A structural formula that sits INSIDE a ruled table cell cannot be a $$…$$ array, because a display block cannot live in a Markdown cell. Draw it with
line breaks and escaped \| for the vertical bonds, and use   runs for the horizontal offsets — literal spaces collapse inside a cell and slide the substituents onto the wrong carbons. The contract's no-pipe-drawing rule applies to free-standing formulas, not to ones trapped in a grid.

In table (1 – 3) on p15 every substituted row draws the vertical bond as a short stroke under its carbon, with the substituent (Cl, Br, H) on the line below. The stroke is real print — a read that drops it and lets the substituent sit directly under the chain has lost printed notation. Inside a ruled grid cell the bond is still written as \mid in the math run, per the structural-formula rule above.

Never put a pipe glyph of any kind inside a ruled table's cells. The vertical bond strokes drawn in a structural formula inside a cell are written with the Unicode bar characters — a single bond as ∣ (U+2223) and a C=O double bond as ‖ (U+2016) — never as `\|` or `\|\|`. An escaped pipe still counts as a cell separator when the two reads are compared, so a table that is identical in both reads reports a bogus column-count defect (p40: 7 cells vs 19 cells for the same five printed columns).

observations: The contents pages print a small □ bullet at the head of every entry. It is a decorative list marker, not content: drop it (pp. 4, 5 and 6 are all transcribed without it).

Only the FIRST contents page (p. 4) prints the `الموضـــوع / الصفحة` header row. The continuation contents pages (5, 6) have no header: leave the Markdown header cells empty rather than repeating or composing one.

On the contents pages the unit rows (`الوحدة الثالثة : الكسور الجزئية`, `الوحدة الرابعة : الاحتمالات`) are printed bold and are transcribed with `**...**` inside the table cell; ordinary lesson entries stay plain.

Contents pages (4–7) print a two-column ruled table whose RIGHTMOST printed column is the topic column — confirmed on tables-audit/6.right.webp — so the topic is Markdown column 1 and the page number column 2.

The header row الموضـــوع / الصفحة is printed ONLY on the first contents page (p. 4). The continuation contents pages (5, 6, 7) print no header: use an empty Markdown header row, never a composed `| الموضوع | الصفحة |`.
Every contents row carries a small decorative square bullet (□) at the right edge of its topic cell. It is repeated ornament, not content — drop it, as pages 4 and 5 already do.
Unit rows in the contents table (الوحدة الأولى …، الوحدة الخامسة : الإحصاء) are printed in heavy bold: keep them as `**...**` inside the table cell and do not promote them to a `##` heading.

Unit-opener objective pages (e.g. p9) print a bold centred ordinal line الوحدة الأولى / الوحدة الثانية …: this is an ORDINAL LABEL, not a chapter title — transcribe it as a plain line with no `##` and no `**`, exactly as on the framed chapter-opener pages.
On those pages the bold body-size lines الأهداف :– and يتوقع بعد دراسة هذه الوحدة … على أن : are labels, not headings: no `#` and no `**`.
A parenthesised binomial with an Arabic-letter exponent is written as one math run, `$(س + أ)^ن$` — not as text plus a bare superscript run `(س + أ)$^{ن}$`.

A bold line printed at BODY size and flush to the right margin, ending in a colon and standing on its own line (e.g. الحد الأوسط والحدان الأوسطان : on p43), is a run-in label, NOT a heading: plain text, no ### and no **. Only a bold line that is also CENTRED and larger than the body is a heading, and a sub-title absent from the contents list on pp4–8 is never one of the 72 lesson titles.

Super- and subscript runs built from Arabic symbols are wrapped in a math run — `الحد الأول $ح_{١} = {}^{ن}ق_{٠} س^{ن} أ^{٠}$` — with the Arabic phrase kept outside it; the ⁿقᵣ combination notation is written `{}^{ن}ق_{ر}`. Bare `^` and `_` with no `$` delimiters (used on pp42, 44 and elsewhere) render as literal carets and underscores and are the known residual form, not the target.

The math run stops where the notation stops: a printed line that is only a comma-separated enumeration (`ر = ٠ ، ١ ، ٢ ، ..... ، ن`) carries no super/subscript and stays OUTSIDE `$$`, because the renderer discards the spacing around its Arabic commas.

p54 spells النوع الثانى dotless in the body but النوع الثاني with a dotted ya inside the table header, one line apart — keep each occurrence as drawn; do not harmonise the two.

A bare row of Arabic-Indic numerals printed as a display block (the proto-matrix on p54) is transcribed as plain text lines, not as $$ ... \quad ... $$ — there is no printed math notation to carry, and Arabic-Indic digits stay outside math runs.

Exercise titles here (`تمرين ( ٣ – ٣ )`) are printed bold, CENTRED and larger than the body line that follows, so they take `### ` — not a bold run-in label; the separator between the two numerals is the book's long dash `–`, and the large ornamental `؟` drawn beside the title is decoration and is not transcribed (settled on p99).

In the partial-fractions exercise lists the same-looking denominators are NOT all of the form `( س٢ + ك )٢`: p99 item (٥) prints `( ٤س٢ + ١ )٢` with the coefficient leading. Read each bracket on the crop; do not regularise one item to the shape of its neighbours.

Statistics chapter (pp. 143, 145, 146, 149): the mean formula is printed as a STACKED fraction whose numerator is a Σ carrying ن above and ر = ١ below — transcribe it as $$\overline{س} = \frac{\sum_{ر=١}^{ن} س ر}{ن}$$, never as an inline solidus and never with the summation limits broken out onto lines of their own.
The printed overbar on the mean symbol is \overline{س} inside the math run, not a combining mark on a bare Arabic letter; ∴ before a derived line is \therefore inside the same $$ block.

A two-line cell inside a ruled table (a header such as 'ساعات العمل' set above its symbol 'س') is ONE cell: write the words separated by a space, with no
and no extra row. The line wrap is justification, like kashida, not content.

Summation limits in this book are Arabic symbols set above and below the ∑ (ن above, ر = ١ below). Transcribe them inside the math run as $\sum_{ر=١}^{ن}$ — never as orphan text lines carrying ن and ر = ١ above and below the sentence.

A ruled table cell that prints a label over its symbol (عدد الطلاب over س، عدد الفصول over ك) keeps that line break as
inside the single cell; do not join them with a space and do not split them into two columns.

The statistics chapter pads some products in a ك × س column to a fixed width with a LEADING ZERO (p146 prints ٠٨٤٠ and ٠٦٢٠ beside unpadded ١٩٢، ٤٤٨، ٢٠٤). Keep the leading zeros; never normalise them away.

A summation printed with ن above the ∑ and ر = ١ below it is transcribed as $\sum_{ر=١}^{ن}$ inside the math run — never as free-standing 'ن' and 'ر = ١' text lines above and below the paragraph, which breaks the sentence into fragments.

The frequency-table mean formula (pp. 143, 145, 146, 149) prints a Σ with ن stacked above and ر = ١ stacked below, over a ruled fraction: transcribe it $\sum_{ر=١}^{ن}$ inline and $$\overline{س} = \frac{\sum_{ر=١}^{ن} م ر ك ر}{\sum_{ر=١}^{ن} ك ر}$$ in display — never as a plain solidus, and never as bare "ن" / "ر = ١" lines placed above and below the paragraph.
The lower-bound symbol in this book's median/mode formulas is printed as هـ (ha with its connecting bar), not a bare ه — transcribe it هـ₁, with the subscript outside any math run.
Class-interval cells in frequency tables are printed as ٢٠ – , ٢٥ – (open upper end) with the book's long dash – ; never substitute an ASCII hyphen and never drop the dash.

A header cell whose text wraps onto two lines is wrapping because the column is narrow — transcribe it as one line, with no
.
This book writes cotangent as ظتا (ظ + ت + ا — exactly two tall strokes). At 1000 px render density the ظ and ت fuse and it reads as ظلتا; settle it on a native-density crop and keep ظتا.

An Arabic-letter formula's digit that is raised and set to the LEFT of its letter is an EXPONENT, not a coefficient: in these RTL runs a multiplying digit prints to the RIGHT of the letter. Check direction against the nearest ordinary RTL run (a radicand such as ل + ٥) before calling a digit a coefficient.
p195 prints the (هـ) exercise without its function letter — 'س = ( س ) = ...' where the neighbouring item prints 'ص = د ( ل ) = ...'. Never supply the missing د.

The limit operator is written نها[س ← ٠] — the limit in square brackets on the plain line, never \underset{س ← ٠}{نها} and never inside a $$ block. The print stacks the limit under نها, but Arabic operator words stay outside math runs in this book; only the stacked fraction goes in an inline $\frac{}{}$. Settled on p217 against pp. 216 and 218.

observations: Bold numbered lines of the form «١ /  …» / «٢ /  …» that enumerate the methods announced by the sentence above them are list items, not headings: keep them as bold lines (**…**), exactly as the adjacent «الخطوات :» label is kept. Only the book's own parenthesised numbering — ( ١-٤-٤ ) and the like, printed in red — marks a `###` section heading.

In this book a numbered subsection line such as «١- التجفيف :» is printed bold on a line of its own, above its paragraph — transcribe it as a '### ' heading, not as a bold run-in label. Run-in labels in this book keep body text on the same line.

Landscape tables in this book are printed rotated 90 degrees on a portrait page: restore them by rotating counter-clockwise, which is the direction that puts the start of the Arabic caption (جدول رقم) at the right and the caption above its table. After that rotation the physically bottom header band becomes the RIGHTMOST column, so it is Markdown column 1, and the years run across the header row.

Never mark a whole rotated table [غير مقروء]: the digits are readable in the native-density tile crops and in tables-audit/<N>.right.webp even when the full-page render blurs them. A blanket illegible over a grid is a transcription failure, not a finding.
Decimals with Arabic-Indic digits use the Arabic decimal separator ٫ (U+066B), not a Latin comma — e.g. ٣٫٥ ، ٥٫٥ in the fat-percentage rows.
The dash inside table/figure references ( ٢–٣ ) and before question numbers (١– ، ٢–) is an en dash – , not a hyphen; spacing around it follows the print and varies line to line.
The book prints الآنتاج (with madda) inside table headers where the body text prints الانتاج — transcribe each as printed, do not unify them.
Decimal marks between Arabic-Indic digits are printed as the Arabic decimal separator: write ٫ (U+066B), never an ASCII comma ',' and never the Arabic comma '،' (e.g. ٧٤٫٥، ١٫٦٥).
In table ( ٢-٥ ) on page 114 the fat row prints ٠٣ with no decimal mark where the column would suggest ٣٫٠ — transcribe ٠٣ as printed.

observations: Bold numbered lines of the form «١ /  …» / «٢ /  …» that enumerate the methods announced by the sentence above them are list items, not headings: keep them as bold lines (**…**), exactly as the adjacent «الخطوات :» label is kept. Only the book's own parenthesised numbering — ( ١-٤-٤ ) and the like, printed in red — marks a `###` section heading.

In this book a numbered subsection line such as «١- التجفيف :» is printed bold on a line of its own, above its paragraph — transcribe it as a '### ' heading, not as a bold run-in label. Run-in labels in this book keep body text on the same line.

Landscape tables in this book are printed rotated 90 degrees on a portrait page: restore them by rotating counter-clockwise, which is the direction that puts the start of the Arabic caption (جدول رقم) at the right and the caption above its table. After that rotation the physically bottom header band becomes the RIGHTMOST column, so it is Markdown column 1, and the years run across the header row.

Never mark a whole rotated table [غير مقروء]: the digits are readable in the native-density tile crops and in tables-audit/<N>.right.webp even when the full-page render blurs them. A blanket illegible over a grid is a transcription failure, not a finding.
Decimals with Arabic-Indic digits use the Arabic decimal separator ٫ (U+066B), not a Latin comma — e.g. ٣٫٥ ، ٥٫٥ in the fat-percentage rows.
The dash inside table/figure references ( ٢–٣ ) and before question numbers (١– ، ٢–) is an en dash – , not a hyphen; spacing around it follows the print and varies line to line.
The book prints الآنتاج (with madda) inside table headers where the body text prints الانتاج — transcribe each as printed, do not unify them.
Decimal marks between Arabic-Indic digits are printed as the Arabic decimal separator: write ٫ (U+066B), never an ASCII comma ',' and never the Arabic comma '،' (e.g. ٧٤٫٥، ١٫٦٥).
In table ( ٢-٥ ) on page 114 the fat row prints ٠٣ with no decimal mark where the column would suggest ٣٫٠ — transcribe ٠٣ as printed.

Two-column credit and name lists in this book carry no printed bullet marker: transcribe each entry as a plain line pairing the right-column name with its left-column affiliation using an em dash, not as a Markdown bullet list and never as a table (no rules or shading are printed).

In the imprint's الإخراج الفني والتصميم / تصميم الغلاف band the book prints one more affiliation line (المركز القومي للمناهج والبحث التربوي) than there are names — keep the extra standalone line, do not drop it to make the pairing come out even.

Verse pages in this book print footnote markers as a raised Arabic-Indic digit inside round brackets — ( ١ ) after بِقِيعَةٍ, ( ٢ ) after حُلُولا — and repeat the same raised digit before each note under the rule at the foot of the page. The digit is small but legible in the native-density crops: read it there rather than writing [غير مقروء].

Section labels such as أولاً : and أ) التّشبيه وأنواعه : are printed bold on their own lines at the right margin but at body size; only the centred, larger bold line (e.g. مراجعةُ علم البيان) is a heading. Transcribe the أولاً / أ) labels as ordinary paragraph lines.
Hemistichs of a بيت are separated on one Markdown line by a run of   entities; the number of entities is a layout choice, not printed content, so it is never a disagreement worth adjudicating.
Lettered sub-section labels such as أ) التّشبيه وأنواعه : and ب) التّشبيهُ البليغُ : are printed bold at body size, not as headings — transcribe them as plain paragraphs, never as ### .

Footnote calls are superscript Arabic-Indic numerals in parentheses and their spacing is inconsistent on the same page — ( ١ ) and ( ٣ ) are spaced while (٢) is closed up against the preceding word. Reproduce each call's spacing as printed; do not normalise them.

The printed page number in the footer does not match the image index (image pages/8.webp carries the printed folio ٢). The footer is page furniture and is dropped — do not renumber anything to match it.
The gap between the two hemistichs of a verse is written as three   entities in this book's transcriptions.

In the تدريبات the example verses and آيات are set in a heavier face and individual words are underlined (عليلٌ، سَهَرٌ، يَدْعُوٓاْ on page 28) — the underline is the teaching mark that points at the محذوف. Transcribe it as <u>…</u> in place; do not replace it with ** bold and do not bold the whole line.
Quranic references are printed surah-name (or الآية) then colon then numeral: transcribe them as (مريم الآية :٤٦) and (سبأ :٣٢) — the colon goes before the numeral in the file, never after it.
Do not insert   entities for the wide gaps between hemistichs or before a verse reference; a single ordinary space is the transcription.
Poetry lines are set in heavier display type in this book; transcribe them as plain text without ** ** emphasis.
Quranic quotations carry small waqf marks above the line (ۖ / ۚ / ۗ) that the scans do not resolve; leave them out rather than guessing which mark is printed.

Qur'anic quotations in this book are set in Uthmani script with their waqf marks (ۚ) and the circular end-of-āyah ornament; transcribe the marks that are printed and do not drop them, and write the ornament as ۝ without inventing the number inside it.
Printed dashes that open an example line (– قال تعالى) and the dashes numbering table rows (١–) are kept as text with an en dash, not converted into Markdown bullets or ASCII hyphens.
Elongated kashidas (بــ) are justification artefacts in this book: write the word with a single tatweel (بـ), not a doubled one.
Qur'anic quotations in this book are set in Uthmani orthography — keep ءَامَنُواْ, مَعَهُۥ, لَفِى, ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ, أَلَآ as printed and do not normalise them to plain Arabic spelling.
The numbered circle that closes a Qur'anic verse in this book is an end-of-ayah rosette: transcribe it ۝, never ۞ (rub el hizb).
Lines of poetry are printed in bold in this book — mark them bold, with the two hemistichs on one line separated by spacing filler.
Body lines that open with a printed dash (–) are transcribed as paragraphs beginning with that dash, not as Markdown bullets.

In the جناس/تورية comparison table the book spells the verb حكي with a final ya (حكي الشّاعر ... بصوتٍ حكي الموسيقا) even though its own body paragraph writes حكى — keep both forms as printed; do not normalise to حكى and do not add a ي to make يحكي.
Verse lines that the book sets in bold (e.g. فقالتْ رُحْ بِرَبِّكَ مِن أمامي) are transcribed with ** ** and the gap between hemistichs as plain spaces — never as   entities.
The long dash the book uses as an item marker before قال الشاعر is transcribed as – (en dash), not an ASCII hyphen.
Verse pages set the two hemistichs of a line side by side; separate them with plain spaces and never with HTML such as   or <sup> — no markup is printed in this book.

Footnote reference marks are printed as raised Arabic-Indic digits in parentheses attached to the last word of the line, e.g. وَدَدا(١); transcribe them inline exactly like that, and give the footnote itself at the foot of the page as ( ١ ) ... with the spaces the print shows inside the parentheses.

The Qur'an boxes print a number inside each end-of-ayah ornament (e.g. ۝٩ … ۝١١ on p41); transcribe ۝ followed by the printed number, and use [غير مقروء] after ۝ when the number is too small to read — never drop it and never supply it from the verse sequence.
The Qur'an font in this book sometimes fails to draw the letter ف (p41: تُفلحون and ٱنفضّوا show a gap where ف belongs); never restore the missing letter from the mushaf.
Qur'anic passages in this book print the ayah number inside each end-of-ayah ornament; write it after the mark as ۝١، ۝٢ … — never drop the printed number.
In the al-Muzzammil passage (verse 3) the word نصفه prints with the ف glyph missing (نِّصْ ـهُۥٓ); do not restore it from the mushaf — keep [غير مقروء] or the printed fragment, never نِّصْفَهُۥٓ.

In the green Qur'anic quotations the font sometimes fails to draw a medial ف, leaving a blank gap with only its fatha (p51: وَنِصۡ َهُۥ for نصفه، وَطَآئِ َةٌ for طائفة). That is a print omission, not illegible ink: do not restore the ف and do not write [غير مقروء]; write the letters that are drawn, keep the floating fatha, and report it as a printed error.

The Qur'anic quotations in this book sometimes drop the letter ف entirely (its harakat float over a gap, e.g. أَنْ ُسِكُمْ for أنفسكم, طَآئِ ـَةٌ for طائفة): never restore the word from the mushaf; mark the word [غير مقروء] and report it as a print omission.

Verse-end ornaments in this book print their āyah number inside (۝١٠٧); the number is legible on the native-density crop — write it as ۝ followed by the printed digits, do not drop it and do not mark it illegible.

The book writes the word شيء in two ways, sometimes on the same page: شيء and شئ (hamza on a ya seat, often stretched by kashida, e.g. في شـئ ليس لله on page 111). Write each one the way it is drawn and do not make them match.
Section numbers in headings print the chapter digit first beside the opening bracket, e.g. (٣–٢) and (٣–٢–١); write the parent section in the same digit order as its subsections and use the en dash.

Chapter opener pages print a part label (الباب الأول / الباب الرابع …) above the green chapter-title cartouche. Only the cartouche title (e.g. علوم السنة) is the ## heading, and the الباب line stays plain text.
Chapter opener pages list their sections on lines that begin with a printed asterisk (* الفصل الأول ...). Write it escaped as \* so it stays a literal asterisk and does not become a Markdown bullet.

Section-opener pages print a centred bold الفصل الأول / الفصل الثاني line above the numbered section heading (e.g. p.117 above (٣–٢) الحكم والاجتهاد); it is not a chapter title, so it takes ### like the section heading, never ##.

The scan's font widens the gap after every non-joining letter (و، ا، د، ر، ز), so words look split (قر ار ات، الو لايات، وغير ها); this is letter-spacing, not a word break — write the word unbroken.

A red bold numbered line on its own line under a section heading, styled like that heading (e.g. (١) الأنظمة التي تميل إلي الحرية التجارية :), takes ### ; the lettered items أ/ ب/ that open running text with an underlined term stay plain paragraphs.

Unit opener pages (e.g. الوحدة الثانية / المحاسبة المالية) carry an uncaptioned photo collage below the title: emit it as ![شكل](pages/<N>.webp) with no caption line, and do not list the incidental English text visible inside the photographed documents or screens as labels.

The book uses the Sudanese word حوجة (need), e.g. لا حوجة لقائمة المتاجرة on page 52. Keep حوجة. Do not change it to حاجة, and do not drop the ح.
The body text writes ايجار without hamza while the ledger tables print إيجار with hamza — transcribe each occurrence as drawn.
Amounts followed by جنيه are often printed joined with no space (١٠٠٠٠جنيه) — keep them joined as printed.

The receipts-and-payments statements (قائمة المقبوضات والمدفوعات) print each ruled half as two aligned sub-columns, amount on the right and its label to the left; transcribe them as a 4-column table in printed order (receipts amount | receipts label | payments amount | payments label), with the total ٣٣٠٠٠٠-style row in the amount columns and empty label cells.

Arabic-Indic dates and sums inside RTL lines must be written so that the rendered RTL line matches the print. When the print shows the day next to the preceding word (في ٣١/١٢/٢٠٠٧م as seen on the page), write ٢٠٠٧/١٢/٣١م. When the print shows (٤٥٠٠٠+٥٥٠٠٠) with ٥٥٠٠٠ next to the label, write (٥٥٠٠٠+٤٥٠٠٠). Never reverse the visual order of the print.

Keep worked amounts such as ٤٠.٠٠٠ × $\frac{١٠}{١٠٠}$ outside math mode with × as plain text. Wrapping the whole product in $...$ renders it left-to-right and swaps the amount and the fraction relative to the print.

Cash receipts/payments summaries printed as two unruled columns (مقبوضات on the right, مدفوعات on the left, amounts with only total underlines) are not ruled grids: transcribe the right column fully as lines (amount then label, as printed), then the left column, never as a Markdown table.
The red right-aligned body-size line ending in a colon that opens a paragraph (e.g. الحسابات الختامية في حالة ممارسة نشاط ربحي :) is a run-in label: write it plain, not as a ### heading.

The receipts-and-payments accounts (قائمة حـ/ المقبوضات والمدفوعات) are printed as a framed box split by one vertical rule. Each half has its own amount column and item column, so transcribe the box as a 4-column table (amount | item | amount | item, rightmost printed column first). Do not merge an amount into its item cell. The totals row puts ٣٠٠,٠٠٠ in both amount columns and leaves the item cells empty.

Dates such as ٣١/١٢/٢٠٠١م are printed with the day on the right and the year plus م on the left. In a Markdown file, the string ٢٠٠١/١٢/٣١م (year typed first) displays exactly that way in an RTL line, but ٣١/١٢/٢٠٠١م (day typed first) displays with the day on the left. Both strings are the same printed date, so a re-read that picks the other order is not a real disagreement. Page 65 keeps year-first; page 64 currently stores day-first. Pick one order for the whole book and use it everywhere.

The framed two-half balance boxes in the exercises (item name and amount side by side in each half, one centre rule) are transcribed as 4-column tables: name | amount | name | amount, with the rightmost printed name as column 1; never merge name and amount into one cell.
Exercise titles such as تمرين (٤) are printed centred, bold, blue and larger than body text: mark them ### .
Each exercise title (تمرين رقم (N)) is a centred, bold, blue line set larger than the body. Write it as a `### ` heading, never as plain text.

Blank ledger-form tables (e.g. نموذج (١–١) دفتر يومية وارد الخزينة) print the row numbers ١ ٢ ٣ ٤ stacked inside a single ruled cell with no rules between them: transcribe them as one cell ١
٢
٣
٤ in one body row, not as separate Markdown rows.

Blank ledger forms (نموذج) print stacked row numbers or denominations inside one unruled cell: keep them in one Markdown cell joined with
, and do not split them into rows that the print does not rule.

In the نموذج ledger tables a total label (المجموع) printed in a merged cell that starts at the second column goes in Markdown column 2; leave the rightmost column empty when its cell is printed empty.

A specimen banking document drawn inside a box (cash deposit receipt, cheque, withdrawal slip) under a numbered red caption such as (١–٤) : إيصال إيداع نقدية is a figure: write the image reference with that caption as alt text, the bold caption line, then each printed field label as a bullet in right-to-left, top-to-bottom order. Do not write it as plain paragraphs, and do not make it a Markdown table, because the box has no ruled grid.

Worked zakat and working-capital solutions print assets and liabilities as two side-by-side columns with no rules: they are not tables, and the right-hand column (مجموع الأصول المتداولة) is transcribed in full before the left-hand column (مجموع الخصوم المتداولة), never interleaved line by line.

Red body-size numbered labels ending in a colon (١. البنك الدولي للإنشاء والتعمير :) that enumerate items announced by the preceding sentence (المؤسسات التالية :) are run-in list labels: write them as plain lines, not ### headings.
